// Stage: reads every Telemetry leaderboard CSV in the export folder named on
// UPDATE DATA and returns a record { Rows, Status }. Port of
// scripts/load_leaderboard.py (read_csvs + build_rows); keep the two in step.
// Connection only; PortalInput and LoadStatus read from it.
let
    Cfg = (name as text) =>
        try Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name = name]}[Content]{0}[Column1] otherwise null,

    RawPath = Cfg("LoadFolder"),
    PathText = if RawPath = null then "" else Text.Trim(Text.Trim(Text.From(RawPath)), """"),
    FolderPath =
        if PathText = "" then
            error Error.Record(
                "No export folder",
                "Paste the folder that holds the Telemetry CSVs into the yellow cell on the UPDATE DATA tab, then Refresh All.")
        else if Text.EndsWith(PathText, "\") then PathText
        else PathText & "\",

    MinEligRaw = Cfg("LoadMinElig"),
    MinElig = if MinEligRaw = null or MinEligRaw = "" then null else Number.From(MinEligRaw),

    // PORTAL INPUT row 4, columns A:BO. REVIEW BOARD reads these by position:
    // never reorder.
    Headers = {
        "Player", "Pos (Telemetry)", "Class", "Prev Team", "HT (in)", "WT", "Elig Yrs", "Snaps",
        "Snaps detail", "Hometown", "High School", "Entered", "Committed To", "Top End Speed (mph)",
        "Risk Level", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed", "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Ball Skills",
        "Run Blocking", "Pass Blocking", "Run Ability", "Tackle Breaking", "Get Off", "Pass Rush",
        "Run Defense", "Tackling", "Accuracy", "Max Throw Vel", "Adj Throw Vel", "INT Avoidance",
        "Pocket Awareness", "Target Selection", "Player Impact", "YAC Over Expected",
        "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact", "Separation", "Explosive Run Rate",
        "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness", "Passing Production",
        "Passing Effectiveness", "Rushing Production", "Rushing Effectiveness", "Evasion Rate",
        "Batdowns", "Push", "Disruption", "Run Stops Over Expected", "Stops Allowed Over Expected",
        "Disruption Prevention", "Movement", "Double Team Rate", "Screen Awareness",
        "Play Action Susceptibility", "EPA Per Target", "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk",
        "Target Rate", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed", "Penalty", "Penalty Drawn", "Notes"},
    Extras = {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "Elusiveness", "Source files", "Benchmark 2025"},

    // CSV header -> PORTAL INPUT header, where the names differ.
    Aliases = {
        {"Pos.", "Pos (Telemetry)"}, {"Team", "Prev Team"}, {"Weight", "WT"}, {"Elig.", "Elig Yrs"},
        {"Top End Speed", "Top End Speed (mph)"}, {"Adj. Throw Velocity", "Adj Throw Vel"},
        {"Max Throw Velocity", "Max Throw Vel"}, {"Deceleration", "Decel"},
        {"Completion Rate Over Expected", "Comp Rate Over Expected"}, {"EPA/Target", "EPA Per Target"}},
    Special = {"Height", "Hometown", "State", "PlayerId", "Rank", "#"},

    // Leaderboard position code -> POSITION MAP code.
    PosMap = [
        QB = "QB", RB = "RB", HB = "RB", FB = "RB",
        WR = "WR", OWR = "WR", SWR = "WR", ATH = "WR",
        TE = "TE", Y = "TE", F = "TE", H = "TE",
        OT = "OT", T = "OT", LT = "OT", RT = "OT",
        OG = "OG", G = "OG", LG = "OG", RG = "OG",
        C = "C", OC = "C",
        IDL = "IDL", DL = "IDL", DT = "IDL", NT = "IDL",
        EDGE = "EDGE", DE = "EDGE", LE = "EDGE", RE = "EDGE", UP = "EDGE", DOWN = "EDGE",
        #"OB-LB" = "OB-LB", LB = "OB-LB", ILB = "OB-LB", OLB = "OB-LB",
        MLB = "OB-LB", WLB = "OB-LB", SLB = "OB-LB",
        CB = "CB", LCB = "CB", RCB = "CB", NCB = "CB", SCB = "CB", OCB = "CB",
        SAF = "SAF", S = "SAF", FS = "SAF", SS = "SAF"],

    TextColumns = {"Player", "Pos (Telemetry)", "Class", "Prev Team", "Snaps detail", "Hometown",
        "High School", "Entered", "Committed To", "Risk Level", "Notes"},

    Num = (v) =>
        if v = null then null
        else if v is number then v
        else
            let s = Text.Trim(Text.From(v))
            in if s = "" or s = "-" or s = "---" then null
               else try Number.From(s, "en-US") otherwise s,

    HeightInches = (h) =>
        let
            parts = if h = null then {} else Text.Split(Text.Trim(h), "-")
        in
            if List.Count(parts) = 2 and Text.Length(parts{0}) = 1
            then try 12 * Number.From(parts{0}) + Number.From(parts{1}, "en-US") otherwise null
            else null,

    AllFiles = Folder.Files(FolderPath),
    Csvs = Table.SelectRows(AllFiles, each
        Text.Lower([Extension]) = ".csv" and Text.Lower([Folder Path]) = Text.Lower(FolderPath)),
    FileList = Table.Buffer(Table.Sort(Table.SelectColumns(Csvs, {"Name", "Content"}), {{"Name", Order.Ascending}})),
    CheckedFiles =
        if Table.RowCount(FileList) = 0 then
            error Error.Record("No CSV files",
                "No .csv files in " & FolderPath & ". Download the Telemetry exports into that folder.")
        else FileList,

    Known = Headers & {"Elusiveness"},
    AliasFrom = List.Transform(Aliases, each _{0}),

    ParseFile = (name as text, content as binary, idx as number) =>
        let
            raw = Table.PromoteHeaders(
                Csv.Document(content, [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001, QuoteStyle = QuoteStyle.Csv]),
                [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
            cols = Table.ColumnNames(raw),
            blanks = Table.TransformColumns(raw, {}, each if _ = "" then null else _),
            withPid = Table.SelectRows(blanks, each Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "PlayerId") <> null
                and Text.Trim(Record.Field(_, "PlayerId")) <> ""),
            derived = Table.AddColumn(withPid, "__derived", each [
                PlayerId = Text.Trim([PlayerId]),
                #"Pos (raw)" = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Pos."),
                #"HT (in)" = HeightInches(Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Height")),
                Hometown =
                    let town = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Hometown"),
                        st = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "State"),
                        stt = if st = null then "" else Text.Trim(st)
                    in if town = null then null else if stt <> "" then town & ", " & stt else town]),
            renamed = Table.RenameColumns(Table.RemoveColumns(derived, List.Intersect({cols, Special})),
                List.Select(Aliases, each List.Contains(cols, _{0}))),
            keep = List.Select(Table.ColumnNames(renamed), each List.Contains(Known, _)),
            base = Table.SelectColumns(renamed, keep & {"__derived"}),
            expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(base, "__derived",
                {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "HT (in)", "Hometown"},
                {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "HT (in)", "Hometown"}),
            indexed = Table.AddIndexColumn(expanded, "__row", 0, 1),
            tagged = Table.AddColumn(Table.AddColumn(indexed, "__idx", each idx), "__file", each name)
        in
            [Table = tagged, Headers = cols, Name = name],

    Parsed = List.Transform(
        List.Positions(CheckedFiles[Name]),
        (i) => ParseFile(CheckedFiles{i}[Name], CheckedFiles{i}[Content], i)),

    Combined = Table.Buffer(Table.Combine(List.Transform(Parsed, each [Table]))),
    ValueCols = List.Difference(Table.ColumnNames(Combined), {"PlayerId", "__row", "__idx", "__file"}),

    // First non-blank value per column, in file-name order (as the Python loader).
    Grouped = Table.Group(Combined, {"PlayerId"}, {{"__rec", (g) =>
        let s = Table.Sort(g, {{"__idx", Order.Ascending}, {"__row", Order.Ascending}})
        in Record.FromList(
               List.Transform(ValueCols, (c) => List.First(List.RemoveNulls(Table.Column(s, c)))),
               ValueCols)
           & [#"Source files" = Text.Combine(List.Sort(List.Distinct(s[__file]), Comparer.Ordinal), "; ")]}}),
    Players = Table.FromRecords(
        List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(Grouped), each [PlayerId = [PlayerId]] & [__rec]),
        null, MissingField.UseNull),

    BenchmarkIds = List.Buffer(
        try Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name = "BenchmarkIds"]}[Content][PlayerId] otherwise {}),

    Shaped = Table.FromRecords(
        List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(Players), (r) =>
            let
                rawPos = Record.FieldOrDefault(r, "Pos (raw)"),
                code = if rawPos = null then null else Record.FieldOrDefault(PosMap, rawPos, rawPos),
                withPos = r & [#"Pos (Telemetry)" = code],
                main = Record.FromList(
                    List.Transform(Headers, (h) =>
                        let v = Record.FieldOrDefault(withPos, h)
                        in if List.Contains(TextColumns, h) then v else Num(v)),
                    Headers),
                extra = [
                    PlayerId = r[PlayerId],
                    #"Pos (raw)" = rawPos,
                    Elusiveness = Num(Record.FieldOrDefault(r, "Elusiveness")),
                    #"Source files" = r[#"Source files"],
                    #"Benchmark 2025" = if List.Contains(BenchmarkIds, r[PlayerId]) then "BENCHMARK" else null]
            in main & extra),
        Headers & Extras),

    Kept = Table.SelectRows(Shaped, each
        MinElig = null or ([Elig Yrs] is number and [Elig Yrs] >= MinElig)),
    Sorted = Table.Sort(Kept, {
        {each if [#"Pos (Telemetry)"] = null then "" else Text.From([#"Pos (Telemetry)"]), Order.Ascending},
        {each if [Player] = null then "" else Text.From([Player]), Order.Ascending}}),

    AllHeaders = List.Distinct(List.Combine(List.Transform(Parsed, each [Headers]))),
    Unmapped = List.Select(AllHeaders, each
        not List.Contains(Known, _) and not List.Contains(AliasFrom, _) and not List.Contains(Special, _)),
    RawCodes = List.Distinct(List.RemoveNulls(Players[#"Pos (raw)"])),
    UnknownCodes = List.Select(RawCodes, each not Record.HasFields(PosMap, _)),

    Status = [
        Folder = FolderPath,
        Files = List.Count(Parsed),
        FileNames = Text.Combine(CheckedFiles[Name], "; "),
        PlayersRead = Table.RowCount(Players),
        RowsKept = Table.RowCount(Kept),
        Dropped = Table.RowCount(Players) - Table.RowCount(Kept),
        MinElig = MinElig,
        UnknownCodes = Text.Combine(UnknownCodes, ", "),
        Unmapped = Text.Combine(Unmapped, ", "),
        Benchmark = List.Count(List.Select(Kept[#"Benchmark 2025"], each _ <> null))]
in
    [Rows = Sorted, Status = Status]
=====
// LoadStatus: what the last refresh read, shown on UPDATE DATA.
let
    s = Stage[Status],
    blank = (t) => if t = null or t = "" then "none" else t,
    Rows = {
        {"Last refresh", DateTime.ToText(DateTime.LocalNow(), "M/d/yyyy h:mm tt")},
        {"Folder read", s[Folder]},
        {"CSV files read", s[Files]},
        {"Players in the files", s[PlayersRead]},
        {"Players loaded (Elig. at or above the minimum)", s[RowsKept]},
        {"Players left out (below the minimum Elig.)", s[Dropped]},
        {"2025 benchmark players among them", s[Benchmark]},
        {"Unmapped position codes (these rows show Baylor tab ?; ST is expected)", blank(s[UnknownCodes])},
        {"CSV columns not used (tell Eric if anything shows here)", blank(s[Unmapped])},
        {"Files", s[FileNames]}},
    Result = #table(type table [Item = text, Value = any], Rows)
in
    Result

    Csvs = Table.SelectRows(AllFiles, each
        Text.Lower([Extension]) = ".csv" and Text.Lower([Folder Path]) = Text.Lower(FolderPath)),
    FileList = Table.Buffer(Table.Sort(Table.SelectColumns(Csvs, {"Name", "Content"}), {{"Name", Order.Ascending}})),
    CheckedFiles =
        if Table.RowCount(FileList) = 0 then
            error Error.Record("No CSV files",
                "No .csv files in " & FolderPath & ". Download the Telemetry exports into that folder.")
        else FileList,

    Known = Headers & {"Elusiveness"},
    AliasFrom = List.Transform(Aliases, each _{0}),

    ParseFile = (name as text, content as binary, idx as number) =>
        let
            raw = Table.PromoteHeaders(
                Csv.Document(content, [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001, QuoteStyle = QuoteStyle.Csv]),
                [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
            cols = Table.ColumnNames(raw),
            blanks = Table.TransformColumns(raw, {}, each if _ = "" then null else _),
            withPid = Table.SelectRows(blanks, each Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "PlayerId") <> null
                and Text.Trim(Record.Field(_, "PlayerId")) <> ""),
            derived = Table.AddColumn(withPid, "__derived", each [
                PlayerId = Text.Trim([PlayerId]),
                #"Pos (raw)" = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Pos."),
                #"HT (in)" = HeightInches(Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Height")),
                Hometown =
                    let town = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Hometown"),
                        st = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "State"),
                        stt = if st = null then "" else Text.Trim(st)
                    in if town = null then null else if stt <> "" then town & ", " & stt else town]),
            renamed = Table.RenameColumns(Table.RemoveColumns(derived, List.Intersect({cols, Special})),
                List.Select(Aliases, each List.Contains(cols, _{0}))),
            keep = List.Select(Table.ColumnNames(renamed), each List.Contains(Known, _)),
            base = Table.SelectColumns(renamed, keep & {"__derived"}),
            expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(base, "__derived",
                {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "HT (in)", "Hometown"},
                {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "HT (in)", "Hometown"}),
            indexed = Table.AddIndexColumn(expanded, "__row", 0, 1),
            tagged = Table.AddColumn(Table.AddColumn(indexed, "__idx", each idx), "__file", each name)
        in
            [Table = tagged, Headers = cols, Name = name],

    Parsed = List.Transform(
        List.Positions(CheckedFiles[Name]),
        (i) => ParseFile(CheckedFiles{i}[Name], CheckedFiles{i}[Content], i)),

    Combined = Table.Buffer(Table.Combine(List.Transform(Parsed, each [Table]))),
    ValueCols = List.Difference(Table.ColumnNames(Combined), {"PlayerId", "__row", "__idx", "__file"}),

    // First non-blank value per column, in file-name order (as the Python loader).
    Grouped = Table.Group(Combined, {"PlayerId"}, {{"__rec", (g) =>
        let s = Table.Sort(g, {{"__idx", Order.Ascending}, {"__row", Order.Ascending}})
        in Record.FromList(
               List.Transform(ValueCols, (c) => List.First(List.RemoveNulls(Table.Column(s, c)))),
               ValueCols)
           & [#"Source files" = Text.Combine(List.Sort(List.Distinct(s[__file]), Comparer.Ordinal), "; ")]}}),
    Players = Table.FromRecords(
        List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(Grouped), each [PlayerId = [PlayerId]] & [__rec]),
        null, MissingField.UseNull),

    BenchmarkIds = List.Buffer(
        try Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name = "BenchmarkIds"]}[Content][PlayerId] otherwise {}),

    Shaped = Table.FromRecords(
        List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(Players), (r) =>
            let
                rawPos = Record.FieldOrDefault(r, "Pos (raw)"),
                code = if rawPos = null then null else Record.FieldOrDefault(PosMap, rawPos, rawPos),
                withPos = r & [#"Pos (Telemetry)" = code],
                main = Record.FromList(
                    List.Transform(Headers, (h) =>
                        let v = Record.FieldOrDefault(withPos, h)
                        in if List.Contains(TextColumns, h) then v else Num(v)),
                    Headers),
                extra = [
                    PlayerId = r[PlayerId],
                    #"Pos (raw)" = rawPos,
                    Elusiveness = Num(Record.FieldOrDefault(r, "Elusiveness")),
                    #"Source files" = r[#"Source files"],
                    #"Benchmark 2025" = if List.Contains(BenchmarkIds, r[PlayerId]) then "BENCHMARK" else null]
            in main & extra),
        Headers & Extras),

    Kept = Table.SelectRows(Shaped, each
        MinElig = null or ([Elig Yrs] is number and [Elig Yrs] >= MinElig)),
    Sorted = Table.Sort(Kept, {
        {each if [#"Pos (Telemetry)"] = null then "" else Text.From([#"Pos (Telemetry)"]), Order.Ascending},
        {each if [Player] = null then "" else Text.From([Player]), Order.Ascending}}),

    AllHeaders = List.Distinct(List.Combine(List.Transform(Parsed, each [Headers]))),
    Unmapped = List.Select(AllHeaders, each
        not List.Contains(Known, _) and not List.Contains(AliasFrom, _) and not List.Contains(Special, _)),
    RawCodes = List.Distinct(List.RemoveNulls(Players[#"Pos (raw)"])),
    UnknownCodes = List.Select(RawCodes, each not Record.HasFields(PosMap, _)),

        Files = List.Count(Parsed),
        FileNames = Text.Combine(CheckedFiles[Name], "; "),
        PlayersRead = Table.RowCount(Players),
        RowsKept = Table.RowCount(Kept),
        Dropped = Table.RowCount(Players) - Table.RowCount(Kept),
        MinElig = MinElig,
        UnknownCodes = Text.Combine(UnknownCodes, ", "),
        Unmapped = Text.Combine(Unmapped, ", "),
        Benchmark = List.Count(List.Select(Kept[#"Benchmark 2025"], each _ <> null))]
in

"""Test a self-service (014-016 layout) workbook against a set of leaderboard
export folders, the way Anthony will: stage the CSVs into one flat folder, point
UPDATE DATA at it, Data > Refresh All, then report LOAD STATUS and the board.

Works on a copy (--out, never overwritten); the numbered workbook is untouched.
Excel COM only.

Usage:
  uv run --with pywin32 python scripts/test_load.py --workbook "<016>.xlsx" ^
      --exports "<Drive>/_exports/2026_asof_2026-09-29/fbs" "<Drive>/_exports/2026_asof_2026-09-29/fcs_g6" ^
      --stage "<scratch>/load_2026" --out "<scratch>/016_2026_test_load.xlsx"
"""

import argparse
import shutil

"""check-exports: check Telemetry leaderboard CSVs before they are loaded.

Catches the two ways a hand-made export goes wrong (both seen 2026-10-06):
- Columns missing because they were switched off in the leaderboard view.
  Download CSV writes only the columns on screen, so a hidden Elig. or Tackle
  Breaking simply is not in the file, and the load cannot notice.
- The file was opened and saved in Excel, which turns Height "6-0" into a date
  ("Jun-00"). The loader cannot read those heights.

Each file's position group comes from its Pos. codes (not the file name, which a
person may get wrong), its tab (Player Traits or Advanced Stats) from its
header. Every required column is listed in EXPECTED; the headers were identical
in every 2023-2026 FBS and FCS / G6 export (checked 2026-10-06).

The same check runs inside telemetry_pull.py on every download and, in the
workbook (019 on), on LOAD STATUS (scripts/powerquery/Stage.m). Keep the three
in step.

Usage (from the repo root):
  uv run python scripts/check_exports.py "<folder of CSVs>" [more folders or files]
Exit code 1 if any file has a problem.
"""

import csv
import io
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROSTER = ["PlayerId", "Rank", "Player", "#", "Pos.", "Class", "Elig.", "Height", "Weight", "Team",
          "Hometown", "State", "Snaps"]

# Leaderboard position group -> the Pos. codes its rows carry.
GROUP_CODES = {
    "QB": {"QB"},
    "RB": {"HB", "FB", "RB"},
    "WR": {"OWR", "SWR", "WR"},
    "TE": {"H", "Y", "F", "TE"},
    "OT": {"LT", "RT", "OT", "T"},
    "IOL": {"LG", "RG", "C", "OG", "G"},
    "IDL": {"DT", "NT", "DL"},
    "EDGE": {"UP", "DOWN", "DE", "EDGE"},
    "OB-LB": {"ILB", "OLB", "LB", "UP"},
    "CB": {"OCB", "SCB", "CB"},
    "SAF": {"FS", "SS", "SAF", "SCB"},
}

# Metric columns after the roster columns, per (group, tab), in export order.
EXPECTED = {
    ("QB", "player-traits"): ["Accuracy", "Pocket Awareness", "Target Selection", "INT Avoidance",
                              "Adj. Throw Velocity", "Max Throw Velocity", "Risk Level", "Tackle Breaking",
                              "Play Speed", "Burst", "CoD"],
    ("RB", "player-traits"): ["Run Ability", "Tackle Breaking", "Elusiveness", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed",
                              "Burst", "CoD", "Pass Blocking", "Ball Skills"],
    ("WR", "player-traits"): ["Ball Skills", "Tackle Breaking", "Elusiveness", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed",
                              "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Run Blocking"],
    ("TE", "player-traits"): ["Ball Skills", "Elusiveness", "Run Blocking", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed",
                              "Burst", "CoD"],
    ("OT", "player-traits"): ["Pass Blocking", "Run Blocking"],
    ("IOL", "player-traits"): ["Run Blocking", "Pass Blocking"],
    ("IDL", "player-traits"): ["Run Defense", "Pass Rush", "Get Off", "Tackling"],
    ("EDGE", "player-traits"): ["Pass Rush", "Get Off", "Run Defense", "Tackling", "Play Speed", "CoD"],
    ("OB-LB", "player-traits"): ["Tackling", "Run Defense", "Pass Rush", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed",
                                 "Burst", "CoD"],
    ("CB", "player-traits"): ["Play Speed", "Deep Speed", "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Tackling",
                              "Run Defense"],
    ("SAF", "player-traits"): ["Play Speed", "Deep Speed", "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Tackling",
                               "Run Defense"],
    ("QB", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Passing Production", "Passing Effectiveness",
                               "Evasion Rate", "Batdowns", "Rushing Production", "Rushing Effectiveness",
                               "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed",
                               "Power Speed"],
    ("RB", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Rushing Production", "Rushing Effectiveness",
                               "Explosive Run Rate", "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact",
                               "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness", "YAC Over Expected",
                               "Separation", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("WR", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness",
                               "Separation", "YAC Over Expected", "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact",
                               "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("TE", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness",
                               "Stops Allowed Over Expected", "Disruption Prevention", "YAC Over Expected",
                               "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty",
                               "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("OT", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Push", "Stops Allowed Over Expected",
                               "Disruption Prevention", "Penalty", "Movement"],
    ("IOL", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Push", "Stops Allowed Over Expected",
                                "Disruption Prevention", "Penalty", "Movement"],
    ("IDL", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Run Stops Over Expected", "Push", "Disruption",
                                "Double Team Rate", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Batdowns",
                                "Screen Awareness", "Top End Speed"],
    ("EDGE", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Disruption", "Push", "Run Stops Over Expected",
                                 "Double Team Rate", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Batdowns",
                                 "Screen Awareness", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed"],
    ("OB-LB", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Screen Awareness", "EPA/Target",
                                  "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk", "Target Rate", "Penalty", "Push",
                                  "Double Team Rate", "Play Action Susceptibility", "Top End Speed",
                                  "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("CB", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "EPA/Target", "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk",
                               "Target Rate", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("SAF", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "EPA/Target", "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk",
                                "Target Rate", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
}

HEIGHT = re.compile(r"^\d-\d{1,2}$")


def group_of(codes):
    """Position group whose codes cover the most rows; None if under 90%."""
    total = sum(codes.values())
    if not total:
        return None
    best = max(GROUP_CODES, key=lambda g: sum(n for c, n in codes.items() if c in GROUP_CODES[g]))
    share = sum(n for c, n in codes.items() if c in GROUP_CODES[best]) / total
    return best if share >= 0.9 else None


def tab_of(group, header):
    """The tab whose expected columns overlap the header most."""
    cols = set(header)
    return max(("player-traits", "advanced-stats"),
               key=lambda t: len(cols & set(EXPECTED[(group, t)])))


def check_rows(header, rows, group=None, tab=None):
    """Problems with one export as a list of strings ([] = fine), plus (group, tab)."""
    problems = []
    if not rows:
        return ["no rows"], (group, tab)
    group = group or group_of(Counter(r.get("Pos.") or "" for r in rows))
    if group is None:
        missing = [c for c in ROSTER if c not in header]
        return ([f"missing columns: {', '.join(missing)}"] if missing else []) + \
            ["position group not recognised from Pos. codes"], (None, tab)
    tab = tab or tab_of(group, header)

"""check-exports: check Telemetry leaderboard CSVs before they are loaded.

Catches the two ways a hand-made export goes wrong (both seen 2026-10-06):
- Columns missing because they were switched off in the leaderboard view.
  Download CSV writes only the columns on screen, so a hidden Elig. or Tackle
  Breaking simply is not in the file, and the load cannot notice.
- The file was opened and saved in Excel, which turns Height "6-0" into a date
  ("Jun-00"). The loader cannot read those heights.

Each file's position group comes from its Pos. codes (not the file name, which a
person may get wrong), its tab (Player Traits or Advanced Stats) from its
header. Every required column is listed in EXPECTED; the headers were identical
in every 2023-2026 FBS and FCS / G6 export (checked 2026-10-06).

The same check runs inside telemetry_pull.py on every download and, in the
workbook (019 on), on LOAD STATUS (scripts/powerquery/Stage.m). Keep the three
in step.

Usage (from the repo root):
  uv run python scripts/check_exports.py "<folder of CSVs>" [more folders or files]
Exit code 1 if any file has a problem.
"""

import csv
import io
import re
import sys
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

ROSTER = ["PlayerId", "Rank", "Player", "#", "Pos.", "Class", "Elig.", "Height", "Weight", "Team",
          "Hometown", "State", "Snaps"]

# Leaderboard position group -> the Pos. codes its rows carry.
GROUP_CODES = {
    "QB": {"QB"},
    "RB": {"HB", "FB", "RB"},
    "WR": {"OWR", "SWR", "WR"},
    "TE": {"H", "Y", "F", "TE"},
    "OT": {"LT", "RT", "OT", "T"},
    "IOL": {"LG", "RG", "C", "OG", "G"},
    "IDL": {"DT", "NT", "DL"},
    "EDGE": {"UP", "DOWN", "DE", "EDGE"},
    "OB-LB": {"ILB", "OLB", "LB", "UP"},
    "CB": {"OCB", "SCB", "CB"},
    "SAF": {"FS", "SS", "SAF", "SCB"},
}

# Metric columns after the roster columns, per (group, tab), in export order.
EXPECTED = {
    ("QB", "player-traits"): ["Accuracy", "Pocket Awareness", "Target Selection", "INT Avoidance",
                              "Adj. Throw Velocity", "Max Throw Velocity", "Risk Level", "Tackle Breaking",
                              "Play Speed", "Burst", "CoD"],
    ("RB", "player-traits"): ["Run Ability", "Tackle Breaking", "Elusiveness", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed",
                              "Burst", "CoD", "Pass Blocking", "Ball Skills"],
    ("WR", "player-traits"): ["Ball Skills", "Tackle Breaking", "Elusiveness", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed",
                              "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Run Blocking"],
    ("TE", "player-traits"): ["Ball Skills", "Elusiveness", "Run Blocking", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed",
                              "Burst", "CoD"],
    ("OT", "player-traits"): ["Pass Blocking", "Run Blocking"],
    ("IOL", "player-traits"): ["Run Blocking", "Pass Blocking"],
    ("IDL", "player-traits"): ["Run Defense", "Pass Rush", "Get Off", "Tackling"],
    ("EDGE", "player-traits"): ["Pass Rush", "Get Off", "Run Defense", "Tackling", "Play Speed", "CoD"],
    ("OB-LB", "player-traits"): ["Tackling", "Run Defense", "Pass Rush", "Play Speed", "Deep Speed",
                                 "Burst", "CoD"],
    ("CB", "player-traits"): ["Play Speed", "Deep Speed", "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Tackling",
                              "Run Defense"],
    ("SAF", "player-traits"): ["Play Speed", "Deep Speed", "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Tackling",
                               "Run Defense"],
    ("QB", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Passing Production", "Passing Effectiveness",
                               "Evasion Rate", "Batdowns", "Rushing Production", "Rushing Effectiveness",
                               "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed",
                               "Power Speed"],
    ("RB", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Rushing Production", "Rushing Effectiveness",
                               "Explosive Run Rate", "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact",
                               "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness", "YAC Over Expected",
                               "Separation", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("WR", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness",
                               "Separation", "YAC Over Expected", "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact",
                               "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("TE", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness",
                               "Stops Allowed Over Expected", "Disruption Prevention", "YAC Over Expected",
                               "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty",
                               "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("OT", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Push", "Stops Allowed Over Expected",
                               "Disruption Prevention", "Penalty", "Movement"],
    ("IOL", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Push", "Stops Allowed Over Expected",
                                "Disruption Prevention", "Penalty", "Movement"],
    ("IDL", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Run Stops Over Expected", "Push", "Disruption",
                                "Double Team Rate", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Batdowns",
                                "Screen Awareness", "Top End Speed"],
    ("EDGE", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Disruption", "Push", "Run Stops Over Expected",
                                 "Double Team Rate", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Batdowns",
                                 "Screen Awareness", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed"],
    ("OB-LB", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "Screen Awareness", "EPA/Target",
                                  "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk", "Target Rate", "Penalty", "Push",
                                  "Double Team Rate", "Play Action Susceptibility", "Top End Speed",
                                  "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("CB", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "EPA/Target", "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk",
                               "Target Rate", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
    ("SAF", "advanced-stats"): ["Player Impact", "EPA/Target", "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk",
                                "Target Rate", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"],
}

HEIGHT = re.compile(r"^\d-\d{1,2}$")


def group_of(codes):
    """Position group whose codes cover the most rows; None if under 90%."""
    total = sum(codes.values())
    if not total:
        return None
    best = max(GROUP_CODES, key=lambda g: sum(n for c, n in codes.items() if c in GROUP_CODES[g]))
    share = sum(n for c, n in codes.items() if c in GROUP_CODES[best]) / total
    return best if share >= 0.9 else None


def tab_of(group, header):
    """The tab whose expected columns overlap the header most."""
    cols = set(header)
    return max(("player-traits", "advanced-stats"),
               key=lambda t: len(cols & set(EXPECTED[(group, t)])))


def check_rows(header, rows, group=None, tab=None):
    """Problems with one export as a list of strings ([] = fine), plus (group, tab)."""
    problems = []
    if not rows:
        return ["no rows"], (group, tab)
    group = group or group_of(Counter(r.get("Pos.") or "" for r in rows))
    if group is None:
        missing = [c for c in ROSTER if c not in header]
        return ([f"missing columns: {', '.join(missing)}"] if missing else []) + \
            ["position group not recognised from Pos. codes"], (None, tab)
    tab = tab or tab_of(group, header)
    missing = [c for c in ROSTER + EXPECTED[(group, tab)] if c not in header]
    if missing:
        problems.append(f"missing columns: {', '.join(missing)}")
    bad = [h for h in (r.get("Height") or "" for r in rows) if h.strip() and not HEIGHT.match(h.strip())]
    if bad:
        problems.append(f"{len(bad)} unreadable heights (e.g. {bad[0]!r}; was the file saved in Excel?)")
    return problems, (group, tab)


def read(path):
    text = Path(path).read_bytes().decode("utf-8-sig")
    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(text))
    rows = list(reader)
    return reader.fieldnames or [], rows


def main(argv):
    if not argv:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    files = []
    for a in argv:
        p = Path(a)
        files += sorted(p.glob("*.csv")) if p.is_dir() else [p]
    if not files:
        sys.exit("No .csv files found.")
    bad = 0
    seen = Counter()
    for f in files:
        header, rows = read(f)
        problems, (group, tab) = check_rows(header, rows)
        seen[(group, tab)] += 1
        label = f"{group or '?'} {tab or '?'}"
        if problems:
            bad += 1
            print(f"PROBLEM  {f.name}  [{label}, {len(rows)} rows]")
            for p in problems:
                print(f"         - {p}")
        else:
            print(f"ok       {f.name}  [{label}, {len(rows)} rows]")
    gaps = [f"{g} {t}" for (g, t) in EXPECTED if not seen[(g, t)]]
    print(f"\n{len(files)} files, {bad} with problems.")
    if gaps:
        print(f"Not in this set (fine if you meant to skip them): {', '.join(gaps)}")
    if bad:
        print("Fix: in the Telemetry leaderboard turn every column on, Download CSV again, "
              "and do not open the file in Excel before loading.")
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

@echo off
rem pull_week: the weekly Telemetry pull in one step.
rem   Downloads all 44 leaderboard CSVs (FBS, then FCS + Group of Six; 11 groups x
rem   Player Traits + Advanced Stats) into ONE dated folder on Drive, checks every
rem   file (check_exports.py), and copies the folder path to the clipboard for the
rem   UPDATE DATA tab.
rem
rem   scripts\pull_week.bat            pull the current season
rem   scripts\pull_week.bat 2026       pull a given season
rem   scripts\pull_week.bat login      log in to Telemetry once (you type the password)
rem
rem   Keep the Chrome window it opens visible until it finishes. Run it again the
rem   same day to retry anything that failed: files already pulled are skipped.
setlocal
set "REPO=%~dp0.."
set "EXPORTS=G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting\_exports"
set "UV=%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\uv.exe"
if not exist "%UV%" set "UV=uv"
set "PULL="%UV%" run --no-project --with playwright python "%REPO%\scripts\telemetry_pull.py""

if /i "%~1"=="login" (
  %PULL% --login
  goto :eof
)

for /f %%d in ('powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd"') do set "TODAY=%%d"
set "SEASON=%~1"
if "%SEASON%"=="" set "SEASON=%TODAY:~0,4%"
set "OUT=%EXPORTS%\%SEASON%_asof_%TODAY%"
echo Pulling season %SEASON% into "%OUT%"
echo.

echo === FBS ===
%PULL% --season %SEASON% --scope FBS --out "%OUT%"
set "FBS_RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
echo.
echo === FCS + Group of Six ===
%PULL% --season %SEASON% --scope "FCS,Group of Six" --tag fcs-g6 --out "%OUT%"
set "FCS_RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
echo.

echo === Checking the files ===
"%UV%" run --no-project python "%REPO%\scripts\check_exports.py" "%OUT%"
set "CHECK_RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
echo.

if not "%FBS_RC%%FCS_RC%%CHECK_RC%"=="000" (
  echo NOT READY. Some files failed or have problems ^(see above^).
  echo Run scripts\pull_week.bat %SEASON% again to retry; files already pulled are skipped.
  exit /b 1
)
<nul set /p "=%OUT%" | clip
echo READY. 44 files in:
echo   %OUT%
echo That path is on the clipboard. In the workbook: UPDATE DATA, paste it into the
echo yellow folder cell, then Data ^> Refresh All ^(2-4 minutes^).

@echo off
rem pull_week: the weekly Telemetry pull in one step.
rem   Downloads all 44 leaderboard CSVs (FBS, then FCS + Group of Six; 11 groups x
rem   Player Traits + Advanced Stats) into ONE dated folder on Drive, checks every
rem   file (check_exports.py), and copies the folder path to the clipboard for the
rem   UPDATE DATA tab.
rem
rem   scripts\pull_week.bat            pull the current season
rem   scripts\pull_week.bat 2026       pull a given season
rem   scripts\pull_week.bat login      log in to Telemetry once (you type the password)
rem
rem   Keep the Chrome window it opens visible until it finishes. Run it again the
rem   same day to retry anything that failed: files already pulled are skipped.
setlocal
set "REPO=%~dp0.."
set "EXPORTS=G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting\_exports"
set "UV=%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\uv.exe"
if not exist "%UV%" set "UV=uv"
set "PULL="%UV%" run --no-project --with playwright python "%REPO%\scripts\telemetry_pull.py""

if /i "%~1"=="login" (
  %PULL% --login
  goto :eof
)

for /f %%d in ('powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd"') do set "TODAY=%%d"
set "SEASON=%~1"
if "%SEASON%"=="" set "SEASON=%TODAY:~0,4%"
set "OUT=%EXPORTS%\%SEASON%_asof_%TODAY%"
echo Pulling season %SEASON% into "%OUT%"
echo.

echo === FBS ===
%PULL% --season %SEASON% --scope FBS --out "%OUT%"
set "FBS_RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
echo.
echo === FCS + Group of Six ===
%PULL% --season %SEASON% --scope "FCS,Group of Six" --tag fcs-g6 --out "%OUT%"
set "FCS_RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
echo.

echo === Checking the files ===
"%UV%" run --no-project python "%REPO%\scripts\check_exports.py" "%OUT%"
set "CHECK_RC=%ERRORLEVEL%"
echo.

if not "%FBS_RC%%FCS_RC%%CHECK_RC%"=="000" (
  echo NOT READY. Some files failed or have problems ^(see above^).
  echo Run scripts\pull_week.bat %SEASON% again to retry; files already pulled are skipped.
  exit /b 1
)
<nul set /p "=%OUT%" | clip
echo READY. 44 files in:
echo   %OUT%
echo That path is on the clipboard. In the workbook: UPDATE DATA, paste it into the
echo yellow folder cell, then Data ^> Refresh All ^(2-4 minutes^).

from pathlib import Path
p = Path("powerquery/Stage.m"); s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
lit = Path("../.m_literals.tmp").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
check = r'''
    // Column check (019): a column switched off in the leaderboard view is simply not
    // in the file, and Excel turns a saved Height "6-0" into "Jun-00". Port of
    // scripts/check_exports.py check_rows: group from Pos. codes (90%+ of rows), tab
    // from the header, then every required column and every Height.
    HeightOk = (h) =>
        let t = if h = null then "" else Text.Trim(Text.From(h)),
            p = Text.Split(t, "-")
        in t = "" or t = "-" or t = "---" or
           (List.Count(p) = 2 and Text.Length(p{0}) = 1 and Text.Length(p{1}) >= 1 and Text.Length(p{1}) <= 2
            and Text.Select(t, {"0".."9", "-"}) = t),
    CheckFile = (cols as list, rows as table) as list =>
        let
            codes = if List.Contains(cols, "Pos.") then
                    List.Transform(Table.Column(rows, "Pos."), each if _ = null then "" else Text.Trim(Text.From(_)))
                else List.Repeat({""}, Table.RowCount(rows)),
            total = List.Count(codes),
            names = Record.FieldNames(GroupCodes),
            cover = List.Transform(names, (g) =>
                List.Count(List.Select(codes, each List.Contains(Record.Field(GroupCodes, g), _)))),
            topN = if total = 0 then 0 else List.Max(cover),
            group = if total > 0 and topN / total >= 0.9 then names{List.PositionOf(cover, topN)} else null,
            overlap = (t) => List.Count(List.Intersect({cols, Record.Field(Expected, group & "|" & t)})),
            tab = if group = null then null
                else if overlap("advanced-stats") > overlap("player-traits") then "advanced-stats"
                else "player-traits",
            need = Roster & (if group = null then {} else Record.Field(Expected, group & "|" & tab)),
            missing = List.Select(need, each not List.Contains(cols, _)),
            heights = if List.Contains(cols, "Height") then Table.Column(rows, "Height") else {},
            badHeights = List.Count(List.Select(heights, each not HeightOk(_)))
        in
            if total = 0 then {"no rows"}
            else (if List.IsEmpty(missing) then {} else {"missing " & Text.Combine(missing, ", ")})
                & (if group = null then {"position group not recognised"} else {})
                & (if badHeights > 0 then {Text.From(badHeights) & " unreadable heights (saved in Excel?)"} else {}),

'''
anchor = "    Num = (v) =>"
assert anchor in s and "CheckFile" not in s
s = s.replace(anchor, lit + check + anchor, 1)
old = "            blanks = Table.TransformColumns(raw, {}, each if _ = \"\" then null else _),"
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, "            blanks = Table.Buffer(Table.TransformColumns(raw, {}, each if _ = \"\" then null else _)),")
old = "            [Table = tagged, Headers = cols, Name = name],"
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, "            [Table = tagged, Headers = cols, Name = name, Problems = CheckFile(cols, blanks)],")
old = "        Benchmark = List.Count(List.Select(Kept[#\"Benchmark 2025\"], each _ <> null))]"
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, old[:-1] + ''',
        ProblemFiles = List.Count(List.Select(Parsed, each not List.IsEmpty([Problems]))),
        Problems = Text.Combine(List.Transform(List.Select(Parsed, each not List.IsEmpty([Problems])),
            each [Name] & ": " & Text.Combine([Problems], "; ")), " | ")]''')
s = s.replace("// Stage: reads every Telemetry leaderboard CSV", "// Stage: reads and checks every Telemetry leaderboard CSV", 1)
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8")

p = Path("powerquery/LoadStatus.m"); s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old = '''        {"CSV columns not used (tell Eric if anything shows here)", blank(s[Unmapped])},'''
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, old + '''
        {"Column check (a PROBLEM file: turn every column on in Telemetry, Download CSV again, do not open it in Excel)",
            if s[ProblemFiles] = 0 then "OK: every file has all its columns"

"""add-column-check: build 019 from 018 with the export column check on LOAD STATUS.

2026-10-06 a staff export came in without Elig. and Tackle Breaking (columns
switched off in the leaderboard view; Download CSV writes only the columns on
screen) and with heights Excel had turned into dates. Nothing in 018 noticed.
019 changes only:
- Power Query Stage and LoadStatus (scripts/powerquery/): every file is checked
  for its required columns and readable heights (port of check_exports.py), and
  LOAD STATUS gains a "Column check" row: OK, or PROBLEM with the file and what
  is missing.
- UPDATE DATA steps 1 and 3 and the README DATA LOAD note say so.
The workbook is refreshed on the same 44 2025 CSVs 018 shipped with, so every
player value is unchanged; the export folder cell is left as it was (empty).

Excel COM only (openpyxl saves strip the conditional formatting). Refuses to
overwrite --out.

Usage:
  uv run --with pywin32 python scripts/add_column_check.py --src "<018>.xlsx" --out "<scratch>/019 ....xlsx" ^
      --exports "<Drive>/_exports/2025_baseline/fbs" "<Drive>/_exports/2025_baseline/fcs_g6" ^
      --stage "<scratch>/load_2025_for_019"
"""

import argparse
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

PQ = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "powerquery"

STEP1 = ("In Telemetry (Leaderboards), open Player Traits, pick the season, scope and a position group, and "
         "check that every column is turned on (Download CSV writes only the columns on screen). Then More "
         "options (...) > Download CSV. Do the same on Advanced Stats. Repeat for every position group you want "
         "(22 files covers all 11 groups). File names do not matter. Do not open the CSVs in Excel first: saving "
         "them turns heights like 6-0 into dates.")
STEP3_ADD = (" Then check LOAD STATUS: Column check must read OK. A PROBLEM names the file and what is missing; "
             "download that file again with every column on.")
README_ADD = (" On every refresh LOAD STATUS checks each file for its required columns (Elig., every trait) "
              "and readable heights (019).")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--src", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--exports", nargs="+", required=True, help="the CSV folders the source was loaded from")
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True, help="new local folder the CSVs are copied into")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    out, stage = Path(args.out), Path(args.stage)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {out}")
    stage.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    n = 0
    for folder in args.exports:
        for f in sorted(Path(folder).glob("*.csv")):
            shutil.copy2(f, stage / f.name)
            n += 1
    print(f"staged {n} CSVs in {stage}")
    shutil.copy2(args.src, out)

    import win32com.client
    xl = win32com.client.DispatchEx("Excel.Application")
    xl.Visible = False
    xl.DisplayAlerts = False
    try:
        wb = xl.Workbooks.Open(str(out))
        for name in ("Stage", "LoadStatus"):
            wb.Queries(name).Formula = (PQ / f"{name}.m").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        ud = wb.Worksheets("UPDATE DATA")
        ud.Range("B6").Value = STEP1
        b8 = ud.Range("B8").Value
        if STEP3_ADD.strip() not in b8:
            ud.Range("B8").Value = b8 + STEP3_ADD
        readme = wb.Worksheets("README")
        cell = readme.UsedRange.Find("PORTAL INPUT is filled by Power Query")
        if cell is None:
            raise SystemExit("README DATA LOAD note not found")
        if README_ADD.strip() not in cell.Value:
            cell.Value = cell.Value + README_ADD

        folder_cell = wb.Names("LoadFolder").RefersToRange
        kept = folder_cell.Value
        folder_cell.Value = str(stage)
        t0 = time.time()
        wb.RefreshAll()
        xl.CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone()
        xl.Calculate()
        print(f"Refresh All: {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
        folder_cell.Value = kept

        st = ud.ListObjects("LoadStatusTable")
        for item, value in st.DataBodyRange.Value:
            print(f"  {item}: {str(value)[:140]}")
        wb.Save()
        wb.Close(False)
    finally:
        xl.Quit()
    print(f"saved {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {out}")
    stage.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    n = 0
    for folder in args.exports:
        for f in sorted(Path(folder).glob("*.csv")):
            shutil.copy2(f, stage / f.name)
            n += 1
    print(f"staged {n} CSVs in {stage}")
    shutil.copy2(args.src, out)

    import win32com.client
    xl = win32com.client.DispatchEx("Excel.Application")
    xl.Visible = False
    xl.DisplayAlerts = False
    try:
        wb = xl.Workbooks.Open(str(out))
        for name in ("Stage", "LoadStatus"):
            wb.Queries(name).Formula = (PQ / f"{name}.m").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        ud = wb.Worksheets("UPDATE DATA")
        ud.Range("B6").Value = STEP1
        b8 = ud.Range("B8").Value
        if STEP3_ADD.strip() not in b8:
            ud.Range("B8").Value = b8 + STEP3_ADD
        readme = wb.Worksheets("README")
        cell = readme.UsedRange.Find("PORTAL INPUT is filled by Power Query")
        if cell is None:
            raise SystemExit("README DATA LOAD note not found")
        if README_ADD.strip() not in cell.Value:
            cell.Value = cell.Value + README_ADD

        folder_cell = wb.Names("LoadFolder").RefersToRange
        kept = folder_cell.Value
        folder_cell.Value = str(stage)
        t0 = time.time()
        wb.RefreshAll()
        xl.CalculateUntilAsyncQueriesDone()
        xl.Calculate()
        print(f"Refresh All: {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
        folder_cell.Value = kept

        st = ud.ListObjects("LoadStatusTable")
        for item, value in st.DataBodyRange.Value:
            print(f"  {item}: {str(value)[:140]}")
        wb.Save()
        wb.Close(False)
    finally:
        xl.Quit()
    print(f"saved {out}")

## telemetry_pull.py (Telemetry leaderboard CSVs, automated)

Playwright drives the installed Chrome on its own profile
(`%LOCALAPPDATA%\telemetry-pull\chrome-profile`) through the same clicks a person

overwritten; a rerun skips files already there and the manifest merges. The CSV
is taken from the page, not Chrome's download manager (it crashed Chrome here).

tab from the header (file names are ignored), then reports missing columns and
heights Excel turned into dates ("Jun-00"). Download CSV writes only the columns
on screen, so a column switched off in the view is simply absent (2026-10-06:
Elig. and Tackle Breaking). Exit 1 on any problem. `EXPECTED` holds the
required columns; they were identical in every 2023-2026 FBS and FCS / G6 file.

(019 on); keep the three in step.

DATA LOAD note, refreshes on the 44 2025 files 018 shipped with, and leaves
the folder cell empty. Excel COM; never overwrites.

I built both, and this week's data is already pulled and checked. The weekly run is a script, not a skill, so it costs no tokens.

**Your weekly run**

Run this from the repo folder, `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV\PP_Recruiting`:

```
scripts\pull_week.bat
```

1. A Chrome window opens. Leave it visible until the script finishes.
2. It pulls all 44 files (FBS, then FCS + Group of Six) into one folder on Drive, `_exports\2026_asof_<today>`. It checks every file and ends with **READY** or **NOT READY**.
3. On READY, the folder path is already on your clipboard. In the workbook, paste it into the yellow cell on UPDATE DATA, then Data > Refresh All. Make sure the **Column check** row in LOAD STATUS reads OK.

Notes:
- **NOT READY:** run the same command again. Files already pulled are skipped and only the failures are retried.
- **Logged out of Telemetry:** run `scripts\pull_week.bat login` and type your password once.
- **Old season:** `scripts\pull_week.bat 2025`.

**Today's test run**
- The full pull worked: `_exports\2026_asof_2026-10-06\` has 44 files (week 6), and every one passed the check.
- Partway through, my test stopped the run. Rerunning skipped the 30 files already there and finished the rest, so the retry path is tested too.

**The column check now runs in three places**
- **In the pull:** a download with a missing column is rejected.
- **For hand downloads, like your colleague's:** `uv run python scripts/check_exports.py "<folder>"` lists any file that's missing a column or has heights Excel turned into dates.
- **In 019:** LOAD STATUS has a new **Column check** row. When I loaded a copy of 019 with one broken QB file mixed into the 44 files, it read: "PROBLEM in 1 file(s). QB TRAITS (26).csv: missing Elig., Tackle Breaking; 31 unreadable heights."
- The check reads each file's position group from the `Pos.` codes, not the file name. Some groups share columns (CB and SAF are identical, and TE traits are a subset of WR traits), so a WR file with two columns hidden would otherwise pass as TE.

**019 is in the Drive root, not in `Send/` yet**
- It's 018 plus the Column check row, with updated steps on UPDATE DATA ("turn every column on", "don't open the CSVs in Excel"). It holds the same 2025 load and every number matches 018.
- `check_workbook.py` passes. Compared with 017, which hasn't been touched since 9/30, only the intended cells differ (plus the A3 note that was already new in 018).

- **`Send/018` was re-saved today at 4:04 PM with the week-5 data loaded** from `_exports\2026_Workings`. Its formulas are fine, but it's no longer the 018 you shipped. Use 019 for the next send.

Everything is logged in LOG.md, STATUS.md and the AGENTS file table, and the repo changes are committed and pushed (`90087b9`). Next number is 020.

Handoff document for a coding agent (Codex, Claude Code, or any other) picking
up this project cold. Read this file first, then `LOG.md` for how the project
got here. `CLAUDE.md` in this folder only points here, so this file is the single
source. The live state (latest deliverable number, what is next) is in the
repo's `docs/STATUS.md`.

Owner: Eric Rash. Last updated: 2026-10-06.

## Where this project lives

Working folder, Windows:
`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

This is Google Drive, not OneDrive. An earlier copy under

documentation and scripts are version controlled in the companion repo

Mac: `~/DEV/PP_Recruiting`), pushed to `erash11/PP_Recruiting`. Read that repo's
`docs/STATUS.md` before starting a session.

---

## 1. What this project is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
**Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles** with the internal **S.T.A.Q.S.**
grading scale, so incoming transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the
players who deserve a scout's time.

Two inputs, one system:

- The scout's **STAQS grade is the grade of record.**
- Telemetry percentiles are **threshold flags** that say who to review and which
  STAQS factors the data already supports.

Nothing is averaged, weighted, or blended into a composite. That was an explicit
design decision, not an oversight (§5).

Audience for the deliverables is recruiting and personnel staff, not analysts.

---

## 2. Standing rules (do not violate)

1. **Read-only in Telemetry.** Never edit, save, or submit anything in
   app.telemetry.fm. Scraping the rendered UI for read purposes is fine.
2. **Always create new files. Never overwrite.** Deliverables are numbered; as of
   2026-10-06 the latest is `019.` and the next is `020.` (check the repo's
   `docs/STATUS.md`). The master `000. BAYLOR - GRD SCALE.xlsx` is never
   modified under any circumstances.
3. **Do not read Telemetry's auth token or import its internal service
   classes.** Both were tried and are blocked. Scrape the rendered table.
4. **STAQS is the grade of record.** Any data output is labeled a starting point
   for the scout, never a grade.
5. **Append to `LOG.md`** whenever a numbered file is created, a design decision
   is made or reversed, or a technique is proven or ruled out. Newest entries at
   the bottom, absolute dates.

**Scripts live in the repo, not here** (`DEV\PP_Recruiting\scripts\`, see its
README). The workbook is reproducible without the lost `build2.py`: 003 is the
layout, `load_leaderboard.py` loads CSVs into a copy (008),
`add_impact_alerts.py` adds the 2026-09-16 alerts (009), a load onto 009 as
template gives 010, and
`check_workbook.py` validates any build against §5. `load.py` is replaced by
`load_leaderboard.py`.

---

## 4. The S.T.A.Q.S. system

Eight factors, each scored **1 / 3 / 9**, summing to **8-72**.

Five critical factors (all positions): **S**ize, **T**oughness, **A**thletic
Flexibility, **Q**uickness, **S**peed. Plus **3 position-specific** factors. QB
has its own set of 8.

Tiers (also loaded as the Player Grade dropdown in Telemetry Scout Reports >
Settings):

| Grade | Score | Elite traits | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| AA | 60-72 | 7-8 | green `00B050` |
| AL | 48-59 | 5-6 | yellow `FFC000` |
| QS | 40-47 | 3-4 | black `404040` |
| FRP | 30-39 | 1-2 | grey `D8D8D8` |
| LIM | 24-29 | 0-1 | pink `ED6363` |
| NGE | 8-23 (dropdown 0-23) | 0 | red `C00000` |

---

## 5. The bridge (Telemetry to STAQS) — the core algorithm

Implement exactly this. Every constant lives on the workbook **SETTINGS** tab
and must stay editable there rather than hardcoded in formulas.

```
elite trait      := Telemetry percentile >= 75
deficiency       := Telemetry percentile < 25
graded traits    := traits with a numeric percentile for that player
elite share      := elite traits / graded traits
```

Elite share (not raw count) is used because positions carry different numbers of
Telemetry traits — OL has 2, LB has 8 — so a raw count would systematically
punish linemen.

Share maps to a projected band using the GRD SCALE's own elite-trait cut lines:

```
>= .875 (7/8) -> AA
>= .625 (5/8) -> AL
>= .375 (3/8) -> QS
>= .125 (1/8) -> FRP
   0          -> LIM, or NGE when deficiencies exceed elite traits by 2+
                 with no elite share
```

Guards and flags:

- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
- **REVIEW** fires at elite share >= .375 (the QS floor), or when the Speed
  alert or Impact alert fires, for any row with at least one graded trait.
- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed >= 90 ("documented difference making
  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
- **Impact alert** (009, decided 2026-09-16): Player Impact >= 90. Fires on its
  own and turns REVIEW on. Chosen after the validation run caught 6 of 13
  missed QS-or-better players at 90.
- **Low Impact alert** (009): a REVIEW row with Player Impact <= 10. A caution
  note only; it never removes REVIEW.
- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — the GRD SCALE's "must be
  special and offer a role" exception.
- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps. Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
  roughly 100 snaps.
- **Profile REVIEW** (013, decided 2026-09-26): the position's two must-haves
  (SETTINGS POSITION PROFILES) both at or above their floors, 200+ snaps, and
  the position's 2nd-path switch on (OT, OG, C, EDGE). Turns REVIEW on. A blank
  must-have counts as not cleared. Must-have status, Profile and the Diamond
  signal show for every position as information only.

**What data can and cannot grade.** Data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
data-graded.

---

## 6. Workbook structure (003 layout; 010 is current, same layout as 009)

Tabs, in order:

- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
- **SETTINGS** — thresholds (rows 5-12 in 009, including the two alert cut
  points at rows 11-12), band cut lines, simplified size standards by position.
  *All tuning happens here.*
- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes -> Baylor eval tabs -> trait counts.
- **PORTAL INPUT** — the data sheet, columns A:BO (67) plus PlayerId, raw
  position, Elusiveness and source file in BP:BS from 008 on. Grouped as Player
  Traits (all positions, P:AC) / QB Traits (AD:AI) / Advanced Stats (AJ:BN).
  Percentiles 0-100; blank where a position carries no metric. HT in inches
  (6'1" = 73). **REVIEW BOARD reads these columns by fixed position, not by
  header, so never insert, delete or reorder PORTAL INPUT columns.** Load data
  with `load_leaderboard.py`, which maps CSV headers onto the template's
  columns.
- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not hand-edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT
  row. Columns: traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, elite share,
  projected band, REVIEW?, speed alert, size-speed alert, Impact alert and Low
  Impact alert (N:O, 009), critical deficiency, data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH /
  ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values, best and worst trait, plus roster metadata.

**Cell legend:** yellow fill `FFF2CC` with blue text = user input. Black text =
formula.

**House styling** (workbooks and companion docs both): Arial throughout unless
the Baylor-style variant is called for; titles Arial 12pt bold Baylor green
`154734`; subtitles and notes 9pt grey `595959`; table header rows white bold on
`154734`; tier fills per §4. The "Baylor style" variants (003 xlsx, 005 docx)
additionally use NCAA Baylor Bears / Baylor Bears Font display type and
Bahnschrift body, with a black masthead bar. Those fonts render only on a
machine that has them installed; Word substitutes elsewhere.

---

## 7. Telemetry platform notes

Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
scouting platform. Login is the user's; an agent without a browser session
cannot reach it.

- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore. Traits and
  stats appear only after filtering to a position or position group.
- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the Player Grade dropdown, already loaded
  with the six STAQS tiers. Scout reports carry a numeric Score (0-72) plus the
  grade.
- **Documentation** pages (Glossary, Player Traits, Advanced Stats) embed
  signed-URL PDFs from s3 docs.telemetry.fm. The PDFs, not the UI tooltips, are
  the reliable definition source.
- Traits and advanced stats are **0-100 percentiles vs the same position** (FBS,
  2019-present, in-game tracking). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph; QB Risk
  Level is a text label; Tackle Breaking is documented but absent from the
  portal grid; QB decision-making surfaces as "Target Selection"; the DB
  coverage stat surfaces as "EPA/Target".
- High school prospects have **no** Telemetry data. Grade them on the STAQS eval
  keys as usual.

### Scraping the portal (proven 2026-09-02, read-only)

- The table is **virtualized** (~20 rows in the DOM) at 100 rows per page.
  Scroll the table's scroll container, then click "Next page" by aria-label.
  Row key = name + Previous + Entered. About 3 s per page.
- Filter panel: Position combobox (remove chip, type code, click option), "Enter
  snap count" input, date range via calendar. Each calendar month arrow moves
  **two** months; the end date cannot exceed Telemetry's own "today".
- **"Apply Filters" sometimes needs a second click.** Verify the "Filter (n)"
  count afterward.
- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload. The filter survives a
  reload but window state does not, so **export scraped data before reloading.**
- Move big payloads out of the browser as gzip+base64.

---

## 8. Current state (2026-09-16; the repo's docs/STATUS.md is always newer)

- **010** is the current workbook: 2025 FBS (all 136 teams) plus FCS
  leaderboard players with Elig 1+ (12,029), 1,899 REVIEW flags (1,708 with
  150+ snaps), Impact and Low Impact alerts in place. Of those, 3,268 players
  and 635 REVIEW flags (545 with 150+ snaps) are Power Four. Every 009 player
  has identical values in 010.
- **009** is the FCS + Group of Six subset (8,761 players, 1,264 REVIEW).
- **Validation run** (repo `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`): 39 players
  Baylor graded on 000's POST-PORTAL RECAP. Projected band exact for 12, within
  one tier for 28; the data runs low against Power Four grades. With 009's
  alerts, REVIEW catches 21 of 28 QS-or-better players and flags 5 of 11 FRP.
- **Scope of 010:** every 2025 FBS or FCS player who still has eligibility,
  including returning Baylor players with Elig 1+.
- Earlier proof of concept (002 / 003): 3,000 transfer-portal players from
  2026-09-02, 608 REVIEW flags.

Known data caution: the portal grid's Top End Speed had implausible values
(e.g. 39 mph), and the leaderboard's Top End Speed looks like a percentile, not
mph. Verify before quoting it. It feeds no flag.

Teaching case used in the coach-facing docs: **Michael Gravely Jr.** (SAF, Ball
State) — 5 elite of 7 traits, so an AL projection, but Player Impact in the 1st
percentile. The traits-versus-production example.

---

## 9. Next steps for an agent picking this up

The ordered list lives in the repo's `docs/STATUS.md`. As of 2026-09-16:

1. **Review the screening matrix (011)** with Eric, then the staff member.
   Open decisions are listed in the repo STATUS.
2. **Weekly refresh** once 2026 data fills in; the staff member runs it himself.

Done 2026-09-16: the full 2025 FBS pull (010) and the matrix draft (011).

Done since the 2026-09-14 version of this list: the data load is versioned code
(`load_leaderboard.py`), the build is reproducible from 003 plus scripts, and
validation exists (`validate_recap.py` against graded players,
`check_workbook.py` against §5).

Things deliberately out of scope: a weighted composite score, any write
operation against Telemetry, and data-grading of FBI, wiring, keep-ability,
character, or medical.

---

## 10. Conventions for whatever you write

- New deliverables are numbered; the next is `020.` as of 2026-10-06 (confirm in
  the repo STATUS). Never overwrite an existing numbered file, and never touch
  `000.`.
- Scripts go in the repo's `scripts/` folder with plain names, not numbered,
  and not in this Drive folder.
- Workbooks: read with openpyxl, but **write only through Excel COM** (pywin32).
  Saving with openpyxl strips the conditional formatting. The docs were built
  with docx-js.
- Deletion is not permitted from the agent session on this machine. Move
  unwanted files into `_to_delete/` and tell Eric.
- Append a dated entry to `LOG.md` for anything you build or decide.

## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions

`check_workbook.py` validates any build against §5. `load.py` is replaced by

---

## 4. The S.T.A.Q.S. system

Eight factors, each scored **1 / 3 / 9**, summing to **8-72**.

Five critical factors (all positions): **S**ize, **T**oughness, **A**thletic
Flexibility, **Q**uickness, **S**peed. Plus **3 position-specific** factors. QB
has its own set of 8.

Tiers (also loaded as the Player Grade dropdown in Telemetry Scout Reports >
Settings):

| Grade | Score | Elite traits | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| AA | 60-72 | 7-8 | green `00B050` |
| AL | 48-59 | 5-6 | yellow `FFC000` |
| QS | 40-47 | 3-4 | black `404040` |
| FRP | 30-39 | 1-2 | grey `D8D8D8` |
| LIM | 24-29 | 0-1 | pink `ED6363` |
| NGE | 8-23 (dropdown 0-23) | 0 | red `C00000` |

---

## 5. The bridge (Telemetry to STAQS) — the core algorithm

Implement exactly this. Every constant lives on the workbook **SETTINGS** tab
and must stay editable there rather than hardcoded in formulas.

```
elite trait      := Telemetry percentile >= 75
deficiency       := Telemetry percentile < 25
graded traits    := traits with a numeric percentile for that player
elite share      := elite traits / graded traits
```

Elite share (not raw count) is used because positions carry different numbers of
Telemetry traits — OL has 2, LB has 8 — so a raw count would systematically
punish linemen.

Share maps to a projected band using the GRD SCALE's own elite-trait cut lines:

```
>= .875 (7/8) -> AA
>= .625 (5/8) -> AL
>= .375 (3/8) -> QS
>= .125 (1/8) -> FRP
   0          -> LIM, or NGE when deficiencies exceed elite traits by 2+
                 with no elite share
```

Guards and flags:

- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
- **REVIEW** fires at elite share >= .375 (the QS floor), or when the Speed
  alert or Impact alert fires, for any row with at least one graded trait.
- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed >= 90 ("documented difference making
  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
- **Impact alert** (009, decided 2026-09-16): Player Impact >= 90. Fires on its
  own and turns REVIEW on. Chosen after the validation run caught 6 of 13
  missed QS-or-better players at 90.
- **Low Impact alert** (009): a REVIEW row with Player Impact <= 10. A caution
  note only; it never removes REVIEW.
- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — the GRD SCALE's "must be
  special and offer a role" exception.
- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps. Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
  roughly 100 snaps.
- **Profile REVIEW** (013, decided 2026-09-26): the position's two must-haves
  (SETTINGS POSITION PROFILES) both at or above their floors, 200+ snaps, and
  the position's 2nd-path switch on (OT, OG, C, EDGE). Turns REVIEW on. A blank
  must-have counts as not cleared. Must-have status, Profile and the Diamond
  signal show for every position as information only.

**What data can and cannot grade.** Data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
data-graded.

---

## 6. Workbook structure (003 layout; 010 is current, same layout as 009)

Tabs, in order:

- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
- **SETTINGS** — thresholds (rows 5-12 in 009, including the two alert cut
  points at rows 11-12), band cut lines, simplified size standards by position.
  *All tuning happens here.*
- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes -> Baylor eval tabs -> trait counts.
- **PORTAL INPUT** — the data sheet, columns A:BO (67) plus PlayerId, raw
  position, Elusiveness and source file in BP:BS from 008 on. Grouped as Player
  Traits (all positions, P:AC) / QB Traits (AD:AI) / Advanced Stats (AJ:BN).
  Percentiles 0-100; blank where a position carries no metric. HT in inches
  (6'1" = 73). **REVIEW BOARD reads these columns by fixed position, not by
  header, so never insert, delete or reorder PORTAL INPUT columns.** Load data
  with `load_leaderboard.py`, which maps CSV headers onto the template's
  columns.
- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not hand-edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT
  row. Columns: traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, elite share,
  projected band, REVIEW?, speed alert, size-speed alert, Impact alert and Low
  Impact alert (N:O, 009), critical deficiency, data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH /
  ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values, best and worst trait, plus roster metadata.

**Cell legend:** yellow fill `FFF2CC` with blue text = user input. Black text =
formula.

**House styling** (workbooks and companion docs both): Arial throughout unless
the Baylor-style variant is called for; titles Arial 12pt bold Baylor green
`154734`; subtitles and notes 9pt grey `595959`; table header rows white bold on
`154734`; tier fills per §4. The "Baylor style" variants (003 xlsx, 005 docx)
additionally use NCAA Baylor Bears / Baylor Bears Font display type and
Bahnschrift body, with a black masthead bar. Those fonts render only on a
machine that has them installed; Word substitutes elsewhere.

---

## 7. Telemetry platform notes

Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
scouting platform. Login is the user's; an agent without a browser session
cannot reach it.

- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore. Traits and
  stats appear only after filtering to a position or position group.
- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the Player Grade dropdown, already loaded
  with the six STAQS tiers. Scout reports carry a numeric Score (0-72) plus the
  grade.
- **Documentation** pages (Glossary, Player Traits, Advanced Stats) embed
  signed-URL PDFs from s3 docs.telemetry.fm. The PDFs, not the UI tooltips, are
  the reliable definition source.
- Traits and advanced stats are **0-100 percentiles vs the same position** (FBS,
  2019-present, in-game tracking). Exceptions: Top End Speed is raw mph; QB Risk
  Level is a text label; Tackle Breaking is documented but absent from the
  portal grid; QB decision-making surfaces as "Target Selection"; the DB
  coverage stat surfaces as "EPA/Target".
- High school prospects have **no** Telemetry data. Grade them on the STAQS eval
  keys as usual.

### Scraping the portal (proven 2026-09-02, read-only)

- The table is **virtualized** (~20 rows in the DOM) at 100 rows per page.
  Scroll the table's scroll container, then click "Next page" by aria-label.
  Row key = name + Previous + Entered. About 3 s per page.
- Filter panel: Position combobox (remove chip, type code, click option), "Enter
  snap count" input, date range via calendar. Each calendar month arrow moves
  **two** months; the end date cannot exceed Telemetry's own "today".
- **"Apply Filters" sometimes needs a second click.** Verify the "Filter (n)"
  count afterward.
- If the pager shows Next disabled on page 1, reload. The filter survives a
  reload but window state does not, so **export scraped data before reloading.**
- Move big payloads out of the browser as gzip+base64.

---

## 8. Current state (2026-09-16; the repo's docs/STATUS.md is always newer)

- **010** is the current workbook: 2025 FBS (all 136 teams) plus FCS
  leaderboard players with Elig 1+ (12,029), 1,899 REVIEW flags (1,708 with
  150+ snaps), Impact and Low Impact alerts in place. Of those, 3,268 players
  and 635 REVIEW flags (545 with 150+ snaps) are Power Four. Every 009 player
  has identical values in 010.
- **009** is the FCS + Group of Six subset (8,761 players, 1,264 REVIEW).
- **Validation run** (repo `docs/2026-09-16-validation-run.md`): 39 players
  Baylor graded on 000's POST-PORTAL RECAP. Projected band exact for 12, within
  one tier for 28; the data runs low against Power Four grades. With 009's
  alerts, REVIEW catches 21 of 28 QS-or-better players and flags 5 of 11 FRP.
- **Scope of 010:** every 2025 FBS or FCS player who still has eligibility,
  including returning Baylor players with Elig 1+.
- Earlier proof of concept (002 / 003): 3,000 transfer-portal players from
  2026-09-02, 608 REVIEW flags.

Known data caution: the portal grid's Top End Speed had implausible values
(e.g. 39 mph), and the leaderboard's Top End Speed looks like a percentile, not
mph. Verify before quoting it. It feeds no flag.

Teaching case used in the coach-facing docs: **Michael Gravely Jr.** (SAF, Ball
State) — 5 elite of 7 traits, so an AL projection, but Player Impact in the 1st
percentile. The traits-versus-production example.

---

## 9. Next steps for an agent picking this up

The ordered list lives in the repo's `docs/STATUS.md`. As of 2026-09-16:

1. **Review the screening matrix (011)** with Eric, then the staff member.
   Open decisions are listed in the repo STATUS.
2. **Weekly refresh** once 2026 data fills in; the staff member runs it himself.

Done 2026-09-16: the full 2025 FBS pull (010) and the matrix draft (011).

Done since the 2026-09-14 version of this list: the data load is versioned code
(`load_leaderboard.py`), the build is reproducible from 003 plus scripts, and
validation exists (`validate_recap.py` against graded players,
`check_workbook.py` against §5).

Things deliberately out of scope: a weighted composite score, any write
operation against Telemetry, and data-grading of FBI, wiring, keep-ability,
character, or medical.

---

## 10. Conventions for whatever you write

- New deliverables are numbered; the next is `020.` as of 2026-10-06 (confirm in
  the repo STATUS). Never overwrite an existing numbered file, and never touch
  `000.`.
- Scripts go in the repo's `scripts/` folder with plain names, not numbered,
  and not in this Drive folder.
- Workbooks: read with openpyxl, but **write only through Excel COM** (pywin32).
  Saving with openpyxl strips the conditional formatting. The docs were built
  with docx-js.
- Deletion is not permitted from the agent session on this machine. Move
  unwanted files into `_to_delete/` and tell Eric.
- Append a dated entry to `LOG.md` for anything you build or decide.

## Imported Claude Cowork project instructions
</system-reminder>
